Nina (sales): Hey product — large customer (Finly) requested streaming function-call results + partial structured outputs for chat. They need partial results to render interim UI and final structured object for downstream processing.
Matt (support): +1, ticket #34871. Customer currently gets a single fn_call at end which blocks UX. They want incremental tool invocations like: first chunk = tool A args, second chunk = tool B args, final = merged JSON.
Casey (product): Ok. Can you paste an example of what the customer expects for the streamed frames?
Nina (sales): Sure, simplified: ```stream frame 1: {"type":"toolcall","tool":"lookup","args":{"id":123}}
stream frame 2: {"type":"toolcall","tool":"format","args":{"style":"compact"}}
stream frame final: {"type":"final","result":{"id":123,"name":"Acme"}}```
Matt (support): They also asked for structured-schema enforcement so their pipeline can trust fields always show up (schema v1).
Olivia (eng): Important notes: our runtime currently supports partial token streaming and has a stable fn_call model where call is emitted at end. Supporting interleaved toolcall frames means changing how we interpret function boundaries and session-level KV cache. Could add framing envelope for toolcall events.
Casey (product): Tradeoffs we need to weigh: backwards compatibility for existing fn_call clients, SDK ergonomics, cost (more small tool calls = more roundtrips), and SLO impact. Also need launch criteria: acceptance tests, schema validation support, and docs.
Nina (sales): Customer is willing to pilot in Dedicated if we can guarantee <200ms tail latency for streaming frames and a clear migration plan. Pilot could be 6-8 weeks.
Olivia (eng): On feasibility: we can prototype event frames in ~2w, but full rollout (SDK updates, gateway routing, canary + fallback) is more like 8–10w. Big unknown is how batching interacts with many small tool frames — could hurt throughput.
Casey (product): Proposed scope options:
- Minimal: framing only, emit toolcall frames as opaque events; no schema enforcement. (low effort, faster pilot)
- Medium: framing + server-side schema validation + SDK helpers to assemble final JSON. (moderate effort)
- Full: streaming toolcall + schema contracts + rollout tooling (canaries, fallbacks, Dedicated routing). (high effort)
Matt (support): Customer strongly prefers Medium, because they want safety checks out of the box. They don't want to assemble messy partials client-side.
Casey (product): For prioritization — where does this land relative to current roadmap? We have two nearby initiatives: streaming structured outputs for webhooks, and fn_call reliability work. I propose we slot Medium as a Q3 stretch if Eng commits 1 FE + 2 BE for 8 weeks.
Olivia (eng): If prioritized, we need clear acceptance criteria: 1) event framing documented, 2) schema validation API with schema versioning, 3) SDK helper to rehydrate partial frames, 4) latency regression <10% vs baseline under pilot workload, 5) canary rollout plan.
Nina (sales): Finly cares about schema versioning most. They asked for audit logs for toolcalls and optional HMAC-signed final object.
Casey (product): Ok — action items: Nina to confirm pilot SLAs and whether Finly will run Dedicated. Matt to attach ticket details and sample logs. Olivia to estimate eng effort with a short RFC. I'll put this as a candidate for Product backlog and tag as customer-driven priority.
Matt (support): Attached sample logs: https://redwood.corp/seq/34871 (private link)
Olivia (eng): Will write RFC draft by EOW with rough timeline and list of impacted subsystems (runtime framing, gateway, SDKs, observability).
Casey (product): Meeting to finalize scope Friday 10am PT? Everyone good?
Nina (sales): Works for me.
Matt (support): I'll be there.
Olivia (eng): Fine.
SupportBot: Meeting scheduled: product-sync Friday 10:00 PT -> Zoom link posted. :calendar:
